# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ • The heavy liquidation in gold on the last day of February clearly flushed a lot of length from an overbought market. Gold still managed to find some more room to the downside last week, however, dropping another $50 to $1,665 on March 6th. Since then we have seen a gradual recovery, interrupted only by a volatile few hours on Friday afternoon. By the end of the week gold looked to have regained a foothold above $1,700 but in the customary mayhem that followed US non-farm payroll numbers, the price plummeted $20 lower before rebounding $35 the other way as headlines circulated suggesting that the US was preparing for possible military action in the Middle East. Gold’s steady uptrend remained intact and prices ended the week almost exactly where they began, around $1,715. • COMEX positioning in the immediate aftermath of the $100+ drop of two weeks ago tells its own story. Net speculative interest was cut back by a staggering 6.4 million ounces in what was easily the heaviest single-week liquidation for more than four years. Almost half of this total liquidation was of large speculative futures positions, indicating that the price move took out some genuine length from the market. At least in this respect, gold looks wellpositioned • Like gold, silver sustained further heavy losses during the week after the February 29th drop. By Tuesday, March 6th it had lost an additional $2 and at its low had traded below $32.50 for the first time since January. The subsequent recovery saw a tentative recapture of the $34.00 level, although silver experienced the same spike down and back as gold in the wake of Friday’s non-farm payrolls. We noted last week that industrial demand for silver was sluggish. There has been a modest improvement at these recent lower prices, with end users seizing the opportunity to stock up before the price recovers. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **12 March 2012** #### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 #### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 #### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 #### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 #### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **12 March 2012** ## **Gold CFTC data to 6 March 2012; ETF data to 9 March 2012.** ### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Gold still managed to find some more room to the downside last week, however, dropping another $50 to $1,665 on March 6th. Since then we have seen a gradual recovery, interrupted only by a volatile few hours on Friday afternoon. By the end of the week gold looked to have regained a foothold above $1,700 but in the customary mayhem that followed US non-farm payroll numbers, the price plummeted $20 lower before rebounding $35 the other way as headlines circulated suggesting that the US was preparing for possible military action in the Middle East. Gold’s steady uptrend remained intact and prices ended the week almost exactly where they began, around $1,715. Friday’s hypersensitive price action was nonetheless a reminder of the nervousness that persists in the market following the recent drop, and gold will need a steady performance this week if it is to regain some of its lustre for investors; any asset that can behave so mercurially in response to such thin newsflow can hardly be taken seriously as a supposed safehaven. - COMEX positioning in the immediate aftermath of the $100+ drop of two weeks ago tells its own story. Net speculative interest was cut back by a staggering 6.4 million ounces in what was easily the heaviest single-week liquidation for more than four years. Almost half of this total liquidation was of large speculative futures positions, indicating that the price move took out some genuine length from the market. At least in this respect, gold looks well-positioned to rebuild and recover in the weeks ahead. - Overall ETF flows were negligible despite the sudden drop in prices, with a total 88,000 ounces added between March 2-9. SPDR Gold Trust holdings were unchanged, while additions to the ETFS funds accounted for nearly all the additional inflows. ### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Mar12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

By Tuesday, March 6th it had lost an additional $2 and at its low had traded below $32.50 for the first time since January. The subsequent recovery saw a tentative recapture of the $34.00 level, although silver experienced the same spike down and back as gold in the wake of Friday’s non-farm payrolls. We noted last week that industrial demand for silver was sluggish. There has been a modest improvement at these recent lower prices, with end users seizing the opportunity to stock up before the price recovers. Investor appetite has been more subdued by comparison, with many still reeling from the recent moves and understandably reluctant to buy back in just yet. - In our last CFTC report we noted that the remarkable 42 million ounce increase in COMEX long positioning that accompanied silver’s run up to $37.00 looked precarious by virtue of its sheer magnitude, and sure enough this week’s unbroken row of red figures show that all of this length and more was flushed out during the selloff— more than 50 million ounces in total. It

is worth noting however that this is not the heaviest liquidation silver has seen in recent times (there have been weeks where the total has been in the region of 80 million ounces) and so in this sense silver may have weathered the storm a little better than gold. - Silver ETFs have added around 4.5 million ounces to holdings so far in 2012, but inflows and outflows in the larger funds largely offset each other last week and overall additions totalled just 68,000 ounces. ### **Silver Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Mar 12** 375 50 Silver price, $/oz

While gold slipped 2.9% lower from March 5th-6th, platinum fell by more than 5.6% in the same period. Another failed attempt at parity with gold demonstrates the resistance platinum faces in this, and the readiness with which many investors will still trade off the spread when the gap narrows sufficiently. Fundamental drivers were few and far between, with the situation in South Africa having receded to the background. Platinum was largely in thrall to the same macro and techn

ical factors that were driving the gold price. The recovery towards the end of last week brought platinum once more within touching distance of gold, and we expect the spread to take on increasing significance as a price driver in the week ahead. - Long futures positions in platinum on NYMEX contracted by just over 97,000 ounces. This sizeable figure was offset by a 30,000 increase on TOCOM. While the net long position decrease of 65,000 ounces is fairly large by recent standards, it pales in comparison with the 6.4 million ounce liquidation in gold and is further testament to the fact that platinum found more friends than gold in last week’s harsh conditions. - Platinum ETFs saw a very small net outflow of 5,700 ounces—a pause in the recent run of decent buying. ### **Platinum Exchange Investment Jan 10 — Mar 12** 2,500 2,000

- The relative resilience of the palladium price while other precious metals were suffering much heavier losses belies the exchange activity during this period. Net long futures positioning decreased by more than 210,000 ounces—the biggest singleweek drop since late September 2011, on which occasion palladium had dropped by almost $100. - Palladium ETFs saw minor inflows. None of the major funds were sellers and two were unchanged. One gets the feeling that the market has fewer strong views on palladium than on the other metals at present, and is waiting for a decisive move away from $700—in either direction—before making any bolder moves. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** ### **Disclaimer:** This briefing is for our clients’ information purpose only.
